headline: Transport and perturbation models test identifiability of single-cell state transitions
label: Causal Single Cell Transition Modeling
summary: Recent preprints test whether single-cell transition and perturbation models identify causal effects and generalize to held-out targets.
synthesis: The dominant thread is whether causal or transition effects in single-cell and high-dimensional data are identifiable and predictable under realistic evaluation. TempoBridge couples source-conditioned flow matching with minibatch optimal transport to predict population transitions, while UOT-IOT addresses identifiability of signed target-state effects through semi-relaxed inverse optimal transport. Evaluation-focused work tests the limits of these approaches: a linear additive-input operator fails target-held-out prediction on current Perturb-seq screens, and label-free Rashomon sets show that per-cell certification does not beat the baseline margin in simulation. A closed-form cell quota bounds angular error of perturbation directions across four public datasets. Mediation and metabolomic studies extend the theme to pathway-level and assay-dependent inference, so the thread is dominant rather than universal.
